headline: Data Centers Pay Grid Costs
short_summary: This bill mandates large energy users, primarily data centers, to bear the costs of their grid infrastructure upgrades, aiming to reduce residential utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Dominion Energy.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Virginia Bill Aims to Cut Residential Energy Costs
news_summary: A new bill in Virginia aims to shift energy costs onto data centers, which currently use about 20% of Dominion Energy's grid but pay only a portion of the price. Analysts predict this could save residential customers over $5 a month and provide over $8 million in relief for local governments by 2027.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires data centers to publicly report their water consumption, enhancing transparency for environmental and resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local governments, water conservationists, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, championed by Senator Kannan Srinivasan, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage, making the numbers publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to address concerns about the industry's water consumption, with the reporting website expected to be live by January 1, 2027.

headline: Local Data Center Siting Control
short_summary: This bill empowers local governments to regulate data center siting and noise levels through mandatory site assessments, addressing community concerns.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, environmental groups, local governments.
news_headline: Data Centers May Need Noise and Energy Disclosure
news_summary: Under HB153/SB94, facilities requiring 100 megawatts or more are defined as high-energy-use and trigger special-exception submission requirements, likely applying to data centers. Fairfax County staff propose requiring a noise study for schools and residences within 500 feet and an energy-provider statement on anticipated demand and source.
